decisions.executionNote: Begin symmetric elbow-up approach toward the ruler, gradually pitching the grippers downward while staying above the table.
Retry the approach with halved translation and pitch increments after the continuity rejection.
Move inward over the ruler's ends and continue the gradual downward pitch, keeping both wrists high and separated.
Continue the separated overhead approach. Plan to push the ruler flat with both fingertips rather than lift any blocks.
Close the empty grippers and orient them downward for a two-point push on the near edge of the set square.
Finish pitching down and lower cautiously just behind the ruler; use closed fingertips as pushers without grasping cubes.
Test a small coordinated forward push, keeping wrist height fixed and checking whether the ruler translates evenly on the tabletop.
The ruler slid toward the robot rather than forward. Withdraw to its near side with slight clearance before establishing a proper pushing contact.
Clear the ruler completely upward before retracting behind it. The contact geometry is uncertain, so establish a fresh near-side approach.
Increase overhead clearance substantially; the ruler appears to be contacted below the assumed fingertip height. Keep blocks untouched while repositioning.
With the ruler now stationary, position farther behind it and descend away from its edge for a fresh forward push.
Advance both closed grippers together from behind at fixed height to locate the ruler's near edge.
Continue the level near-side approach in small symmetric steps; monitor the ruler for forward translation before pushing farther.
The elevated approach did not move the ruler. Back off slightly and lower the pushers incrementally to engage its near edge rather than pass over it.
Test forward contact at the lower height, moving both pushers evenly and leaving the cubes untouched until the straightedge reaches them.
The straightedge remained stationary under the fingertips. Retreat just behind it and lower another 27 mm to the previously observed contact height.
Make a slow coordinated forward contact test at the lower height; check both ruler ends for even tabletop motion.
Left contact advanced its end, but the right missed and the ruler yawed. Hold the left pusher still and reposition the right behind its lagging end with clearance.
Lower the right pusher behind the lagging end, matching the left contact height and downward orientation without moving the left end.
Advance only the right pusher to catch the lagging end and restore the ruler's horizontal alignment; keep the left contact stationary.
Both contacts are now visible. Bring the right end level with the held left end before resuming a parallel push.
The ruler is nearly level and engaged by both pushers. Advance toward the cubes, correcting the small remaining right-end lag.
Push the flat straightedge evenly toward the staggered cubes, maintaining the established contact height and parallel orientation.
The straightedge has contacted the nearer cubes. Continue slowly until it also engages the farthest cube and squares all three faces.
All three cubes now appear square and aligned against the straightedge. Disengage backward, then raise the empty grippers to begin resetting without disturbing the row.
The row remains aligned after disengagement. Retract both arms toward their own home workspaces while gradually restoring the original wrist pitch.
Continue the smooth elbow-up return, separating the arms toward their original lateral positions while restoring horizontal gripper orientation.
Continue returning toward the initial poses with modest pitch and translation increments. The aligned cubes remain undisturbed.
